blocks.value: Run an OpenSCAP compliance scan on an RHEL 9 instance, verifying system security settings against the CIS profile.

inputs.name: command
inputs.value:
# 1. Install required packages if they are not already installed
sudo dnf install -y openscap-scanner scap-security-guide

# 2. Check if the SCAP content file exists
if [ ! -f /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml ]; then
  echo "SCAP content not found at /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml"
  exit 1
fi

# 3. Verify that the CIS profile exists in the SCAP content
if ! sudo oscap info /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml | grep -qi "cis"; then
  echo "CIS profile not found in SCAP content"
  exit 1
fi

sudo rm -f cis-scan-results.xml

# 4. Run the OpenSCAP scan using the CIS profile
sudo oscap xccdf eval \
  --profile xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_cis \
  --results cis-scan-results.xml \
  /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml | tee oscap_output.log

# 5. Ensure proper file permissions on the results file
sudo chmod 0644 cis-scan-results.xml

blocks.value: Retrieve the XML scan results from the RHEL instance after the OpenSCAP scan completes.
Upload the compliance scan results to the Concert platform for compliance tracking and further analysis.

meta.description: This workflow automates the CIS compliance scan for RHEL 9 using OpenSCAP, ensuring security compliance based on CIS benchmarks. The scan results are retrieved and uploaded into Concert for analysis.
